questions.stem: Aschoff bodies consist of all of the following except:
questions.solutionHtml:
B lymphocytes
  • Aschoff bodies—are composed of foci of T lymphocytes, occasional plasma cells, and plump activated macrophages called Anitschkow cells.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 561, 562

questions.stem: Which of the following statement are true regarding activated macrophages in Aschoff bodies?
questions.solutionHtml:
All of the above

Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 561, 562

questions.stem: All of the following statements are true regarding histological features of rheumatic heart disease except:

options.label: A
options.text: Diffuse inflammation and Aschoff bodies may be found in any of the three layers of the heart

options.label: B
options.text: Subendocardial lesions, McCallum plaques, are usually found in the right atrium

options.label: C
options.text: Leaflet thickening and commissural fusion are seen

options.label: D
options.text: Shortening, thickening, and fusion of the tendinous cords are seen

questions.answerText: Subendocardial lesions, McCallum plaques, are usually found in the right atrium
questions.solutionHtml:
Subendocardial lesions, McCallum plaques, are usually found in the right atrium
  • False, subendocardial lesions, exacerbated by regurgitant jets, can induce irregular thickenings called MacCallum plaques, usually in the left atrium.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 561, 562

questions.stem: All of the following statements are true regarding rheumatic mitral stenosis except:

options.label: A
options.text: Fishmouth or buttonhole deformity is seen

options.label: B
options.text: Left atrium progressively dilates and harbors mural thrombi

options.label: C
options.text: Acute inflammation, with post-inflammatory neovascularization and transmural fibrosis obliterates the leaflet

options.label: D
options.text: Vegetations are seen on either or both sides of the valve leaflets

questions.answerText: Vegetations are seen on either or both sides of the valve leaflets
questions.solutionHtml:
Vegetations are seen on either or both sides of the valve leaflets
  • False, Rheumatic fever phase of rheumatic heart disease (RHD) is marked by small, warty vegetations along the lines of closure of the valve leaflets.
  • Libman-Sacks endocarditis (LSE) has small- or medium-sized vegetation on either or both sides of the valve leaflets.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 561, 562

questions.stemHtml: A 12-year-old male patient had a throat infection two to three weeks back and now presented with fever and joint pain. A cardiac biopsy is shown in the figure, identifying the lesion based on the histological picture.
questions.solutionHtml:
Aschoff bodies
  • History is highly suggestive of RHD, as the patient is a child with a history of throat infection two to three weeks back and now presenting with fever and joint pain. Histopath image is that of Aschoff bodies.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 561, 562
